maya: Quick bring-up of `pleroma-v1` embeddings on int8. Ran a smoke eval against quick-recall holdout and seeing a recall@1 drop vs fp16 baseline. sharing numbers below.

sam: what command/dataset did you run? can you paste the exact eval cmd?

maya: ran:```bash
python eval_embeddings.py \ 
  --model pleroma-v1 \ 
  --quant int8 \ 
  --quant-type per_channel \ 
  --dataset quick_recall_holdout \ 
  --metric recall@1,5,10 
  --norm cosine
```

maya: results: `recall@1=0.716`, `recall@5=0.892`, `recall@10=0.934`. baseline fp16 on same holdout: `recall@1=0.754`.

jun: ugh ~4.8% absolute drop at R@1. what's silhouette/clustering? any centroid drift?

maya: silhouette (kmeans, k=50) fp16=0.28, int8=0.19. centroid cosine shift mean=0.042.

arnaud: did you try L2 vs cosine? sometimes quantization interacts with normalization.

maya: eval used cosine norm. I just re-ran quick L2 check: recall@1 (int8, L2)=0.712 so slightly worse.

liam: any preprocessing differences? float->quant pipeline? need to ensure embeddings are normalized pre-quant.

maya: pipeline: model outputs raw vec -> `l2_normalize` -> quantize. confirmed normalization applied before quantization.

jun: ok next steps: 1) try per-tensor int8 (we used per_channel initially?), 2) run calibration with 2k samples, 3) check SSE of top-k neighbors diff.

arnaud: also try symmetric vs asymmetric quant, and clamp ranges with percentile 99.9. for per-tensor we sometimes see less variance in small dims.

maya: will try. scheduling jobs now. posting job ids.

ops-bot: Job started: `embed-eval-1715123456-pleroma-int8-per-tensor` (eta ~12m) :gear:

sam: also please include eval on longer queries (short queries are more brittle). maybe run shortseq/longseq splits.

maya: queued shortseq/longseq splits in the same job.

liam: if per-tensor reduces recall loss but hurts tail, we can consider partial quant (quantize top 80% dims) or mixed precision (int8 on bulk, fp16 for head dims).

jun: add to the job: compute nearest neighbor overlap (top1/top5) vs fp16 and dump mismatches to s3 `s3://redwood-ml/pleroma/quant-mismatches/1715123456/`

maya: done. will attach mismatch sample ids.

ops-bot: Job finished: `embed-eval-1715123456-pleroma-int8-per-tensor`. Summary: recall@1=0.743, recall@5=0.893, silhouette=0.24. Calibration uses 2048 samples, symmetric quant.

maya: promising — per-tensor + symmetric + 2k calib recovered R@1 to 0.743 (baseline 0.754). still ~1.1% abs gap.

arnaud: good. can we run tiny-magnitude-preserve trick (rescale small dims before quant) next? often fixes centroid drift.

liam: also run a cheap rerun: compute cosine similarity distribution shift (hist) and KL divergence vs fp16. if KL < 0.02 maybe acceptable.

maya: ran KL calc on job output: KL=0.017.

sam: okay that looks within our temporary threshold. propose: mark int8-per-tensor + symmetric + 2k calib as candidate for staging. add a rollback plan: auto-fallback to fp16 on any recall@1 drop > 0.5% in production.

jun: capture evaluation prompts and seed sets as an eval bundle so we can reproduce and include in rollout checklist.

maya: created eval bundle: `eval-bundles/pleroma-v1/int8-per-tensor/1715123456.tar.gz` and uploaded to `gs://redwood-evals/pleroma/`.

liam: add perf numbers too: tokens/sec inference unchanged, embedding throughput ~+22% on int8. cost estimate ~ -18% per-unit.

maya: final note: clustering artifacts mostly from low-variance dims. I'm going to try partial-quant on dims with var < 1e-5 and keep them fp16 next. will report results in this thread. :eyes:

sam: thanks all — great triage. ping me once partial-quant numbers are in and we'll schedule a staging rollout if stable. :thumbsup:
